claims.substep_do: Open the sign-in route and confirm the form asks for an email and a password only
claims.observation: Opened the sign-in view; the form contains exactly two fields—Email (type=email) and Password (type=password)—plus the submit button, with no other requested inputs.

claims.substep_do: Open the sign-up route and confirm a new account can be created from it
claims.observation: Opened the /signup route, submitted a unique display name, email, and valid password, and confirmed successful account creation by reaching the signed-in account page showing QA New Visitor and the new email.

claims.substep_do: Sign in with the first account documented in the app user readme and confirm the account route opens
claims.observation: Signed in with visitor@example.com and confirmed the /account route opened, showing Ada Moreau's account.

claims.substep_do: Sign out and confirm the browser returns to the home route
claims.observation: Clicked Sign out; the browser returned to the home route (/), and the header now shows Sign in instead of the signed-in user.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the top bar carries the logo, the nine route labels and one Get in Touch action
claims.observation: The top bar contains the Zettajoule logo, exactly nine route labels (Company, Technology, Solutions, Our Edge, Our Team, Investors, News, Careers, Contact), and one Get in Touch action; their shared y-position confirms they are in the same top bar.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the foot of the route carries a get-in-touch invitation
claims.observation: The route footer includes a prominent “GET IN TOUCH” invitation with the message “Tell us what you need powered.” and a “Get in Touch” link.

claims.substep_do: Open the home route and confirm the reactor stands on the first screen under one huge display line reading Powering the World
claims.observation: The home route loads with the prominent “Powering the World” hero line on the first viewport and the reactor module artwork positioned directly beneath/behind it.

claims.substep_do: Scroll the home route and confirm the reactor comes apart, exposing a fuel column, and the metal resolves into a line drawing
claims.observation: Scrolling the home route advanced the reactor from sealed through rods/dome separation to “Fuel core exposed,” then to “Resolved to a technical drawing,” confirming both requested states.

claims.substep_do: Confirm the three key facts appear beside the opened reactor naming the reactor type, the module output and the outlet temperature
claims.observation: The opened reactor section shows all three key facts: “High-temperature gas-cooled reactor,” “250 MW thermal a module,” and “750 degrees Celsius at the outlet.”

claims.substep_do: Confirm the home route carries a passage about the company name and a row of industry cards
claims.observation: The home route includes a dedicated “THE NAME” passage explaining why the company is called Zettajoule, followed by “Eight industries, one module family” with industry cards arranged in a row (e.g. Oil and Gas, Chemicals, Transport, Steel).

claims.substep_do: Confirm each stage of the reactor sequence is also readable as plain written text
claims.observation: The page includes a visible “The reactor sequence in words” section listing every stage in plain text: Whole, Rods out, Dome off, Core exposed, and Drawn, each with a written description.

claims.substep_do: Open the company route and confirm the opening line, the vision, the mission, the naming story and the three offices
claims.observation: The /company route shows the opening line “clean heat and electricity to power a world of industrial applications,” dedicated Vision, Mission, and Name story sections, and three offices: Rotterdam (headquarters), Chicago (licensing), and Tokyo (engineering).

claims.substep_do: Open the technology route and confirm the cutaway with the fuel, the graphite, the helium, the digital copy, the safety case and the modules
claims.observation: The /technology route is open and shows the interactive “Open the module” cutaway with component controls, plus sections covering “The fuel,” “Graphite and helium,” “A living digital copy,” “The safety case rests on a real machine,” and “Built in modules.”

claims.substep_do: Drag the technology diagram, then tap one part, and confirm that part explains itself
claims.observation: Moved the technology diagram’s range control to its end state, then selected “Helium circuit”; the page displayed an explanation that helium enters cool, leaves the core at 750°C, crosses a heat exchanger, and is chemically inert.

claims.substep_do: Open the edge route and confirm the modernized proven design, the temperature case, the modules and the business model
claims.observation: Opened the Our Edge route and confirmed it presents the modernized, operating-record-backed design; the 300°C water-cooled versus 750°C Zettajoule temperature case; single- and multi-module deployment; and the owned, operated, staffed energy-supply business model.

claims.substep_do: Open the team route and confirm the opening line over a grid of four leaders on soft tinted plates
claims.observation: The /team route opens successfully with the line “shaping the future of nuclear together” and a four-column leadership grid for Mira Halvorsen, Tobias Ruiz, Anneke Vos, and Daniel Okoye on generated portrait plates.

claims.substep_do: Open one leader profile link, then the view-bio action, and confirm the fuller description opens in the shared modal
claims.observation: Opened Mira Halvorsen’s professional profile link, then selected View bio; the shared dialog opened with her fuller multi-sentence description, profile link, and Close dialog control.

claims.substep_do: Move between two showcase routes and confirm the change does not reload the page and a cover sweeps across

claims.observation: Filter-result replacement is static/immediate in both tested directions, while keyboard focus independently produces the intended short focus-ring animation as the sole captured animation. This matches the criterion.

The reactor state follows scroll position in both directions: it advances through stages while scrolling down, retraces an observed intermediate stage while scrolling up, and returns to whole at the top. The intermediate state also remained stable while waiting, ruling out a once-triggered timed sequence.

The observations show a consistent blue token rgb(47, 111, 237) on company CTAs and several account links, but newsroom story links measured dark rather than blue. The rule requires the home route, explorer, and account route each to reflow cleanly at phone, tablet, and desktop widths with no sideways scroll or overlap. evidence: On the solutions explorer, CDP motion capture started immediately before selecting Industry = Steel and stopped after the count changed to “Showing 1 of 8 solutions”; it recorded animation_count: 0. The resulting URL was /solutions?industry=Steel and the grid contained only the Steel result.

A second capture around Clear filters, settled at “Showing 8 of 8 solutions,” also recorded animation_count: 0, confirming the replacement in the opposite direction had no fade, slide, stagger, or other captured animation.

A separate CDP capture around keyboard focus recorded exactly one animation: name “focus-ring,” duration 220 ms, one iteration, linear. Focus inspection showed the focused input had a solid 3px rgb(47, 111, 237) outline.
active_results.rationale: Filter-result replacement is static/immediate in both tested directions, while keyboard focus independently produces the intended short focus-ring animation as the sole captured animation. This matches the criterion.

evidence: On the home route at the top, the live status read “Sequence: Whole module, sealed.”
Scrolling down one page changed the live status to “Sequence: Control rods withdrawn, dome lifted”; scrolling down again changed it to “Sequence: Resolved to a technical drawing.”
Scrolling back up one page reversed the status from the technical drawing to “Control rods withdrawn, dome lifted,” and scrolling up again returned it to “Whole module, sealed.”
A repeat test from Home to PageDown left the reactor at “Control rods withdrawn, dome lifted” after a 2-second wait, rather than continuing automatically on a timer.
active_results.rationale: The reactor state follows scroll position in both directions: it advances through stages while scrolling down, retraces an observed intermediate stage while scrolling up, and returns to whole at the top. The intermediate state also remained stable while waiting, ruling out a once-triggered timed sequence.

evidence: Verified the three relevant routes directly: /company, /news (title “Newsroom, Zettajoule”), and /account while authenticated as visitor@example.com.
On /company, measured CTA links “See what it powers” and “Get in Touch” at background/border rgb(47, 111, 237) with white text; “See what it powers” bounding box was x=149, y=3377, 203×44.

On /account, measured inline links “Steel,” “Data Centres,” and “Hydrogen sites” at rgb(47, 111, 237), while “Open the document room” used the same rgb(47, 111, 237) as its background/border with white text; “Steel” bounding box was x=137, y=464, 238×26.

On /news, the content links sampled (“First module order signed,” “Helium loop completes a 1000 hour run,” and “Steel partnership targets the hydrogen route”) measured dark text rgb(43, 39, 36), not blue; the featured link’s blue appeared only as border-color rgb(47, 111, 237).

Screenshots were requested for sampled company and newsroom elements, and bounding boxes were measured, but the required pointer-hover state was not captured or measured before evidence collection ended.
active_results.rationale: The observations show a consistent blue token rgb(47, 111, 237) on company CTAs and several account links, but newsroom story links measured dark rather than blue. More importantly, no direct hover-state measurement was obtained, so it is not defensible to determine whether links across all three routes deepen to a darker shade of the same blue under the pointer. Because the required hover comparison remains unobserved, the criterion cannot be resolved.
